![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223529/assets/d4d60c547afdb873c30e6c5e1f70d616dc31ace79b482f37ae51ea4f036d5a42.png)

Calculate ${∮}_{C}\,\text{d}x,$ where $C$ is the closed path along the quarter circle of 
radius $2,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $x$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $x$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1},
$$

where ${x}_{2}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${x}_{1}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, the initial and terminal points are the same (since the path is closed and is traversed only once). Therefore, ${x}_{1}={x}_{2},$ and we have

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}x=0.
$$
